title: Network, media manipulation and the MCA Universal music director
summary: A music executive tells him to love it or leave it.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Did you see the movie Network, by any chance?
It was just shown on TV a few weeks ago and it won an Oscar about two years ago.

There was one really interesting statement, the plot of it is of a fourth television network and how they talk about audience manipulation and what is done in a really outrageous sense to gain an audience. It was written by Paddy Chayevsky.
Oh yeah, I remember that. I didn't see it, I remember it.

The president of the network is making this big, emotional, passionate speech and he said, there are no governments anymore, it's all governed by big business. The world isn't run by government, it's run by corporations.
I guess in a sense if you're talking about manipulation and whatever, without getting paranoid about it, there is that part of life that has to be dealt with.

There was this guy who was director of music, MCA, Universal Studios, a nice guy, but he's in this job and he has to perform this job. He used to be a song plugger at Witmark and he's there now and his function is to get people to work at Universal as cheaply as he possibly can and he does a pretty good job at that too.
I think one day I was complaining about it and he said, if you don't like the way we do things here, why don't you go
off and go to Russia. Well I didn't want to get into a discussion of it and I let it stop there.
No. Either you do it our way or you get out of here.
If you don't like the way we do it you get out.
But they have the tools to do it and that didn't exist anywhere to the degree that it does today, twenty years ago. Hitler showed us how.
